You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {{
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }},
    {{
      "keystrokes": "cd project\\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }}
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used as shell commands.
- Most bash commands should end with a newline (\n) to cause them to execute
- For special key sequences, use: C-c for Ctrl+C, C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies wait time:
- 0.1 seconds for instant commands (cd, ls, echo, cat)
- 1.0 seconds for normal commands (gcc, find, rustc)
- 5-30 seconds for slow commands (make, python scripts, wget)

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are executed in sequence
- Do not include extra whitespace unless it's part of the command
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action
- Set task_complete to true ONLY when the task is fully finished and verified
- CRITICAL: BEFORE writing any code or modifying files, you MUST explore the workspace and read the provided documentation (e.g., `cat skill.md` or `cat task_spec.json`) to learn the required skills and constraints.
- DO NOT rely solely on your pre-trained knowledge. Base your implementation strictly on the context provided in the workspace documents.

Task Description:
You are working in a sprint planning repo. Please create a concise but complete sprint planning package for the following initiative: a new self-service report export feature for end users and administrators. I need one epic breakdown, one prioritized backlog slice, and one sprint plan for a 2-week sprint. Use INVEST-compliant user stories, clear Given-When-Then acceptance criteria, and realistic story points. 

Save your output as three separate .txt files named:
- epic_breakdown.txt
- prioritized_backlog.txt  
- sprint_plan.txt

Keep the output in plain text format that a PO could paste into a planning meeting agenda. 

For the epic_breakdown.txt, explicitly reference the different personas (End User, Administrator) and include acceptance criteria with Given-When-Then format.

For the prioritized_backlog.txt, include clear priority levels (such as High/Medium/Low or Must/Should/Could) and assign story points (using Fibonacci numbers like 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13) to each user story.

For the sprint_plan.txt, include a velocity note based on a team average velocity of 28 points with one developer on 50% PTO this sprint. Clearly specify both "committed" work and "stretch" work sections in your sprint plan.

Ensure all files reference the report export initiative.

================================================================================
EPIC BREAKDOWN: Self-Service Report Export Feature
================================================================================
Initiative: REPORT_EXPORT
Epic ID: EXPORT_PACKAGE
Duration: 2-Week Sprint

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EPIC DESCRIPTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Enable end users and administrators to export filtered reports to PDF and CSV
formats through a self-service interface, with audit trail capabilities for
administrators to track export activity.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PERSONAS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. END USER
   - Need: Export reports to PDF and CSV formats
   - Priority: HIGH

2. ADMINISTRATOR
   - Need: Audit export activity and manage export permissions
   - Priority: HIGH

3. POWER USER
   - Need: Export reports with advanced filters and date ranges
   - Priority: MEDIUM

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
USER STORY BREAKDOWN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STORY E-1: End User - Basic Report Export to CSV
As an End User, I want to export reports to CSV format so that I can analyze
the data in spreadsheet applications.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am viewing a report in the system
  When I click the "Export to CSV" button
  Then I should receive a downloadable CSV file with all report data
  And the file should include column headers matching the report columns


STORY E-2: End User - Basic Report Export to PDF
As an End User, I want to export reports to PDF format so that I can share
and print reports with stakeholders.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am viewing a report in the system
  When I click the "Export to PDF" button
  Then I should receive a downloadable PDF file with the report formatted
  And the PDF should include the report title and export timestamp


STORY E-3: Power User - Export with Filters
As a Power User, I want to apply filters before exporting so that I only
export the specific data I need.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am viewing a report with available filters
  When I apply filters and click "Export"
  Then the exported file should only contain data matching my filter criteria
  And the export should include a note about applied filters


STORY E-4: Power User - Export with Date Range
As a Power User, I want to specify date ranges before exporting so that I
can export data for specific time periods.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am viewing a time-series report
  When I select a date range and click "Export"
  Then the exported file should only contain data within my selected range
  And the date range should be visible in the export file metadata


STORY A-1: Administrator - View Export Audit Log
As an Administrator, I want to view an audit log of all report exports so
that I can track who exported what and when.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am an Administrator accessing the audit dashboard
  When I navigate to the Export Audit section
  Then I should see a list of all export activities
  And each entry should show: user, report name, format, and timestamp


STORY A-2: Administrator - Filter Export Audit Log
As an Administrator, I want to filter the export audit log so that I can
investigate specific export activities.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am viewing the export audit log
  When I filter by user, date range, or report type
  Then the audit log should display only matching entries
  And I should be able to clear filters to see all entries again


STORY A-3: Administrator - Manage Export Permissions
As an Administrator, I want to control which users can export reports so
that I can enforce data governance policies.

Acceptance Criteria:
  Given I am an Administrator managing user permissions
  When I enable or disable export permissions for a user or role
  Then the permission change should take effect immediately
  And users without export permissions should not see export options

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TECHNICAL TASKS (Non-Functional)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
T-1: Implement export service layer with PDF and CSV generation
T-2: Design and implement audit logging database schema
T-3: Add export permission checks to authorization layer
T-4: Write unit tests for export functionality
T-5: Write integration tests for audit logging

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEPENDENCIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- PDF generation library integration
- CSV encoding for special characters
- Audit log storage capacity planning

================================================================================
EOF\n",
